# Results — Study 240 (Dividend-Initiation) on real annual panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Event study: firms paying
their FIRST dividend (from yfinance `.dividends` history) vs matched non-initiator
non-payers and vs the equal-weight full basket. Signal year = first year with annual
dividends ≥ $0.01/share; forward return = next-calendar-year auto-adjusted total return.
As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Bias warning (top of results)

**Survivorship bias is intentional and named on the Signal axis.** The 50-name universe
consists of large-cap US stocks alive as of 2026-06-16, mixing established payers with
growth names that historically were non-payers. Companies that went bankrupt, were
acquired, or fell out of large-cap status are absent. Furthermore, the control arm
(non-payers) is dominated by hyper-growth tech names (AMZN, TSLA, NVDA…) that had
extraordinary returns over 2000-2025 — making the "initiator vs control" comparison a
comparison against an extremely high hurdle, not a matched cohort.

## Data stamp

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Source | Yahoo Finance (`yfinance`, `yf.Ticker(t).history(period="max", auto_adjust=True)` + `.dividends`) |
| Universe | 50 large-cap US stocks (survivorship-biased; mix of established payers + non-payers) |
| Panel years | 2000 – 2025 |
| Initiation definition | First calendar year with annual dividend sum ≥ $0.01/share |
| Forward return | Calendar year *y+1* auto-adjusted (total-return) close-to-close return |
| Events in sample | 8 initiation events across 8 distinct calendar years (2003–2025 window) |
| Panel fingerprint | `2c284615386a` |
| As-of | 2026-06-16 |

| 2012 | AAPL | +8.1% |
| 2016 | NVDA | +81.9% |
| 2024 | GOOG, CRM, META | +19.4% (avg) |

Note: most pre-2000 initiations are outside the signal window (e.g., WMT initiated 1990,
HD 1991). Events in 2025 do not have forward returns available.

## Arm summary

| Arm | n years | Mean return | Vol | Sharpe | HAC *t* vs 0 | Hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Initiators (first div yr)** | 8 | **+28.4%/yr** | 34.4% | **+0.83** | **+3.57** | 88% |
| Control (non-payers, same year) | 8 | +40.9%/yr | 50.7% | +0.81 | +6.52 | 81% |
| EW basket (initiator years only) | 8 | +26.4%/yr | 16.6% | +1.59 | +4.84 | 100% |

*Note: all arms have high raw t-stats because they include bull-market years. The EW basket
and control arm means are inflated by survivorship and by the extraordinary run in tech
stocks (NVDA +82%, V +68% etc. are in the control universe prior to initiation).*

## The honest test — initiator spread

| Comparison | n years | Mean spread | HAC *t* | Inference |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| Initiators vs control (non-payers) | 8 | **−23.1%/yr** | **−2.45** | Significant — **wrong direction** |
| Initiators vs EW basket | 8 | **+2.1%/yr** | **+0.40** | **Not significant** |

- **Initiators vs EW (+2.1%/yr, t = +0.40)**: the natural comparison — does dividend
  initiation predict higher-than-average returns vs the full basket? No. Eight data points
  give a t-stat of 0.40, far below the |t| ≥ 2 bar. The point estimate is positive but
  economically noisy and statistically invisible.
- **Initiators vs control (−23.1%/yr, t = −2.45)**: the control arm is not a proper
  matched cohort — it is an equal-weight basket of pure non-payers (AMZN, TSLA, NVDA,
  SNAP, DDOG…) that massively outperformed over this period. A statistically significant
  *negative* spread here says initiators underperformed the hyper-growth tech basket, not
  that initiation destroys value. This number is a selection-bias artifact.
- **Events per year**: 0 in most years (median = 0, max = 3). With so few events, the
  initiator arm return is effectively a small portfolio of individual firm draws, not a
  diversified signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine works when there is something to find

On the deterministic synthetic panel (`data.synthetic_panel`), the same engine recovers an
initiation premium **only when one is planted**, and reads near 0 in the null:

| Planted premium (%/yr) | Spread detectable? |
|---:|:---:|
| 0% (null) | no |
| 10% | marginally |
| 15% | in larger samples |

The real spread of +2.1%/yr vs EW is well inside the noise band at n = 8.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The HAC t-stat on the initiator-vs-EW spread is +0.40 at n = 8
  years of events. There is no statistically significant re-rating premium following
  dividend initiation in this large-cap universe.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Fewer than 3 events per year in a 50-name universe leaves no
  room for diversification; real costs (bid-ask, market impact) would consume any spread;
  and the universe has survivorship bias baked in from construction.
- **vs EW — No Edge.** Initiators earn +2.1%/yr over the EW basket — statistically
  indistinguishable from zero at this sample size.
